newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG volcano calms, but leaves six dead.
newsitem.headline: PNG volcano calms, but leaves six dead.

text.p: A state of alert on the Papua New Guinea island of Manam was scaled down on Thursday after a volcanic erupution subsided, leaving six people dead and at least 29 injured.
About 1,000 people were evacuated by boat to the mainland on Wednesday as lava flowed down to the sea, destroying three of the island's nine villages, emergency services officials said.
However, the evacuation was halted late Wednesday as volcanic activity eased.
"It's now relatively quiet," said Leith Anderson, director of the National Disaster and Emergency Services in Port Moresby.
"There are parts of the island that weren't as badly damaged as we thought so we'll be able to shift people around and rebuild things," Anderson told Reuters.

Anderson said two people were killed by flying debris, a child died on the way to hospital suffering from burns, and a fourth person was found dead in the sea at the bottom of a lava flow. Two other people died from unspecified injuries after being taken to a health centre on the mainland.
Ash had also affected most of the gardens and food crops on the island, which is home to 7,000 people, he said.
Manam island is 15 km (nine miles) off the northeast coast of Papua New Guinea and last erupted in both 1991 and 1992.
The South Pacific island nation's emergency services have been monitoring the volcano since it erupted again three-and-a-half weeks ago, spewing rock and lava into the sea.

Papua New Guinea is on the Pacific's volcanic belt called the "Ring of Fire". Rabaul, a port town located on New Britain island 800 kms (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby, was devastated in September 1994 when two volcanoes on either side of the town erupted, forcing the evacuation of 30,000 residents.
